assertion: In SIBO subjects (>=10^3 CFU/mL on MAC), specific bacterial strains show distinct symptom correlation profiles. E. coli BL21(DE3): abdominal pain r=0.284 (P=.049), diarrhea r=0.321 (P=.02), bloating r=0.110 (sig). E. coli K-12: abdominal pain r=0.337 (sig), diarrhea r=0.298 (sig), excess gas r=0.348 (sig), urgency r=0.374 (sig). K. aerogenes KCTC 2190: abdominal pain r=0.374 (P=.013), diarrhea r=0.305 (P=.038), excess gas r=0.286 (P=.048). Escherichia is more associated with bloating and diarrhea; Klebsiella has a greater association with abdominal pain.

subject.name: E. coli and K. aerogenes strains

qualifiers.magnitude: Spearman r values 0.110-0.374 across strain-symptom pairs; see assertion for full matrix; all reported P<.05
qualifiers.conditions: shotgun metagenomic sequencing of duodenal aspirates; symptom severity measured by VAS 0-100; SIBO defined as >=10^3 CFU/mL on MAC
qualifiers.population: n=28 subjects with shotgun data (N=17 SIBO >=10^3, N=11 non-SIBO <10^3); mean age 61+/-16y
qualifiers.model: human prospective cross-sectional (REIMAGINE study shotgun subset)

provenance.ref: Leite et al. Defining Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth by Culture and High Throughput Sequencing
provenance.location: Results — Specific Coliform Strains section, p.266; Table 2, p.267; Discussion p.268
provenance.original_text: only specific E coli strains, with genomic similarities to E coli BL21(DE3) and E coli strain K-12 substrain W3110, correlated with abdominal pain (Spearman r = 0.284, P = .049; and Spearman r = 0.337, P = .02, respectively), and diarrhea (Spearman r = 0.321, P = .030; and Spearman r = 0.298, P = .04, respectively); a specific K aerogenes strain, with genomic similarities to K aerogenes KCTC 2190, correlated with abdominal pain (Spearman r = 0.374; P = .013), diarrhea (Spearman r = 0.305; P = .038), and excess gas (Spearman r = 0.286; P = .048)... Escherichia is associated with bloating and diarrhea, whereas Klebsiella has a greater association with abdominal pain

integrity.coi_detail: Pimentel lab. Small shotgun subset (n=28) limits statistical power. Multiple comparisons across many strain-symptom pairs increase false discovery risk.
integrity.methodology_note: Shotgun subset is small (n=28). Correlations are modest (r=0.11-0.37). Multiple strain-symptom comparisons were performed; FDR correction status for these specific correlations is unclear from text. Cross-sectional design cannot establish causality.
